about: Agent-facing index of the scene kit's STABLE props and its scene presets. Use these ids in a scene_stage or clipart block; never write SVG. Generated by gen_catalogue.py.

conventions.x: Left to right, 0 to stage.width (a preset's width is in its layout; a custom stage is 600..4000). The camera views a window of stage.zoom units, so with a pan camera keep the action inside 0..width.
conventions.y: 0 is the ground line; NEGATIVE is up, positive is toward the viewer. A ground-mounted prop needs no y. Wall items (clocks, screens, paintings) need a negative y (about -300 to -500 in an interior); interior ceiling lights use y -620.
conventions.lane_y: Movers (walk, ride, drive, fly, hover, orbit) use y as a lane: 40 to 120 passes in FRONT of buildings and props standing on the ground line; y near 0 puts them behind. lane_y is what the preset layouts use for that prop.
conventions.scale: Multiplies the listed size. Most props read well at the listed scale (typically 1.5 to 2.5 outdoors). size is width and height in scene units before scale.
conventions.mount: ground = stands on y 0; wall = give an explicit negative y; ceiling = hangs from the interior ceiling; sky = celestial or cloud (drawn automatically, do not place); centred = its origin is its middle, give an explicit y.
conventions.moves: The motions a prop suits as an actor. If absent, place it as scenery. Aircraft add takeoff (roll, rotate, climb; ry is the climb height) and land (descend, flare, roll out).
conventions.time: theme.time has four values: dawn (early morning), day (midday and afternoon), dusk (evening), night.
conventions.sketch: When no prop fits, a scenery or actors item may carry sketch instead of prop: an array of SVG element strings (rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path, g; fill/stroke as #hex; one element per string; no text, style or href), drawn with its origin at the ground point like a prop, up negative. Use it to add a missing object to a scene; prefer a listed prop when one fits.

rules: Use `label` instead of `prop`/`sketch` on a scenery or actors item to draw REAL text: a plain string, drawn by trusted code, never agent-authored markup (no injection surface, unlike sketch).
Split multi-line text with \n: up to 4 lines, each 1..40 characters, 160 characters total. Longer text should be shortened, not wrapped by the renderer.

`size` (8..80, default 26) is the font size in scene units. `colour` is #rrggbb or an @palette name (same names as sketch_style.colours), default @dark. `align` is start|middle|end (default middle). `bold` is true/false.
The item's y is the text's OWN baseline (its bottom), matching every prop's ground/attach-point convention; multiple lines stack UPWARD from there.
A label can be an actor too (it moves like any other actor on its motion), but it is never a registry prop: no variant, no anchors, no `moves`.
Origin is the ground contact point, bottom-centre; up is negative. Props are 40 to 150 units wide (a person is 44 x 92, a sofa 144 wide): draw at that size and use scale for anything bigger.

Outlines are applied for you (dark, 2.4 wide, round joins and caps). Only add stroke-width for thick limbs: draw a thick dark stroke (5 to 7) and a thinner coloured stroke on top, as the kit does for legs.
Colour with palette names in fill and stroke, written @name: they follow day and night and match the props. Closed shapes with no fill get a light fill.
Build an object from 6 to 14 simple shapes: body, head, limbs as thick round strokes, then two or three small details (eye, nose, highlight). Flat colours; no gradients, no text.

Animate lightly. Give the whole item anim {kind: sway|bob|spin|pulse|blink|drift, period, amount}, or hand-write animateTransform / animate for a custom motion (a wagging tail, a bouncing squash-and-stretch ball, an irregular decaying arc).

A hand-written animate or animateTransform is NEVER its own sketch array entry: it has nothing to animate on its own. Put it as a CHILD, inside the same <g> as the shape(s) it moves, e.g. one string '<g><animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" values="0 0;0 -20;0 0" dur="1s" repeatCount="indefinite"/><circle cx="0" cy="0" r="10" fill="@red"/></g>', not two separate strings.

To reuse a REAL prop's artwork instead of drawing it, put '<use href="#a-<id>">' (or '<use href="#a-<id>--<variant>">') inside a sketch element -- only real, existing ids/variants are accepted, checked against the same asset index. Wrap it in an animated <g> like any shape to give it custom motion a preset or built-in actor motion cannot.

conventions.extending a preset: Give preset plus scenery_add / actors_add to append props to a preset's layout instead of rewriting it; scenery / actors replace the preset's list.
